messages.subject: Dealing with multiple hierarchies
messages.body_plain:
Hello hbayesdm-users,

I’m hoping to apply the ug_delta model to estimate individual
learning rates from an ultimatum game. However, there are two groups
of participants (older vs younger adults), and each participant
experiences three different conditions while playing the game. In the
end I would like to estimate one learning rate for each participant
during each condition. If I understand correctly, the documentation
suggests that to compare different groups I should be fitting
separate models for each group
(https://ccs-lab.github.io/hBayesDM/articles/getting_started.html#compare-models-and-groups),
but I was unsure of the best way to handle the conditions within
groups. Should I fit three models,
one for each condition, and just pull out the individual parameters?
Or should I fit six different models, one for each group*condition?
Or just one model but give each subject*condition a unique
identifier?

Each of these methods ignores some of the
hierarchical information but I wanted to be extra careful that the
parameters don’t get biased by ignoring some of this information.
We ultimately want to answer the question of whether there is a
group*condition interaction in learning rate (i.e., norm adaptation).
So, our plan was to take the individual estimates and feed them into
a 2x3 ANOVA.

Thanks for any advice!

Jeff

messages.subject: Re: Reinforcement Learning with 3 trial types
messages.body_plain:
Dear Cynthia,
I was wondering whether you ever managed to implement this three choice probabilistic learning task in stan, as I am trying to do exactly the same - probabilistic learning task (30/70) with three stimuli types - reward, punishment, neutral.
If so, would you be able to advice me how you implemented this?
Thanks,
Franziska

>
>
>
> If I’m separating 3 trial types and do separate model parameter estimations for them, should I code differently for 3 trial types? For example,

> Reward trials: win (1), non-win (0)

> Punishment trials: non-loss (0), loss (-1)

> But it then becomes a problem for neutral trials. In neutral trials, 2 outcomes are both neutral (0). But people sometimes grew a preference for one of the two. We would like to tease that piece out. Would it make sense that we always use 1 and -1 for 3 runs of the model? In other words, win, non-loss, and one of the neutral outcome will be 1, and non-win, loss, and the other neutral outcome will be -1, in their respective models.

Can we run a separate model estimation for each condition (e.g. fitting the prl_rp model 3 times to reward, neutral, and punishment trials)? If that's the case, should I differentiate in the Outcome column by using 1, 0, and -1? Or it's okay to use 1 as winning/avoid losing, and -1 as no-win and losing money?
